title: Exploiting Code Symmetries for Learning Program Semantics

layout.note: Two unframed panels side by side, each titled by a letter and a name under it. Inside each panel the same top-down pipeline: a code box and its permuted copy joined by a dashed g arrow, r arrows down to two rows of coloured embedding squares joined by g (or h), then p arrows to the predicted name with a tick or cross. Panel (a) adds thin dashed curves from every statement to its embedding.

lesson: Draw an invariance claim as a commutative square: the transformation g on the input and the same g on the representation, one changed element tracked in red through both, ending in tick versus cross, while the baseline lane breaks the square (h ≠ g).
